gloss: to standardize; to make uniform; to homogenize

definitions.gloss: to make a group of things, people, or systems all the same — in form, content, or treatment — regardless of individual differences; to standardize, to make uniform, to homogenize
definitions.explanation: To forcibly bring a varied group into a single uniform shape, often with a negative nuance of ignoring individuality or local differences. The word is most commonly used to criticize overly uniform education, fashion, architecture, or business practices that suppress diversity. It is often translated as 'standardize' or 'homogenize,' but unlike neutral English 'standardize,' Japanese {画一化|かくいつか}する usually implies 'flatten into sameness' rather than 'bring up to a quality standard.'

examples.japanese: ⟦{教育|きょういく}→教育：01313_kyouiku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{画一化|かくいつか}する。
⟦{街|まち}→街：17306_machi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風景|ふうけい}→風景：03591_fuukei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{画一化|かくいつか}されてしまった。
⟦{製品|せいひん}→製品：01445_seihin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{品質|ひんしつ}→品質：09507_hinshitsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{画一化|かくいつか}することで、⟦{不良|ふりょう}→不良：11320_furyou⟧⟦{率|りつ}→率：03802_ritsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げた→下げる：00807_sageru⟧。
examples.english: We lowered the defect rate by standardizing product quality.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{個性|こせい}→個性：11536_kosei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{無視|むし}して→無視する：17288_mushisuru⟧{画一化|かくいつか}するような⟦{教|おし}え{方|かた}→教え方：28588_oshiekata⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{創造性|そうぞうせい}→創造性：05214_souzousei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{育|そだ}たない→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧。
examples.english: Creativity cannot grow under a style of teaching that ignores children's individuality and tries to make everyone alike.

notes:
Composed of {画一|かくいつ} (uniform, identical) + ⟦{化|か}→〜化：28335_ka⟧ (-ization, a common suffix turning a noun into a verb meaning 'to make into') + ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧. {画一|かくいつ} itself is built from {画|かく} ('stroke, line') + {一|いつ} ('one'), originally evoking the idea of drawing everything with a single line — all exactly the same.

USAGE:
- Object + ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{画一化|かくいつか}する: to standardize / homogenize [object]
- Subject + ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{画一化|かくいつか}する (intransitive usage): to become uniform
- The passive {画一化|かくいつか}される is very common, as this kind of flattening is typically felt as something that happens to a system rather than something someone actively chooses.
{画一化|かくいつか}する often carries a critical or negative tone — the speaker is complaining that individuality and diversity are being lost. When it is used in a positive technical sense (e.g., standardizing manufacturing quality), the neutral word ⟦{標準化|ひょうじゅんか}→標準化：20534_hyoujunka⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ is usually preferred.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{教育|きょういく}→教育：01313_kyouiku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{画一化|かくいつか}する: to make education uniform
- {街並|まちな}み⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{画一化|かくいつか}する: (for) townscapes to become homogenized
- ⟦{品質|ひんしつ}→品質：09507_hinshitsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{画一化|かくいつか}する: to standardize quality (neutral / positive nuance)
- ⟦{価値観|かちかん}→価値観：10431_kachikan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{画一化|かくいつか}→画一化：22353_kakuitsuka⟧: homogenization of values
- ⟦{文化|ぶんか}→文化：01504_bunka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{画一化|かくいつか}→画一化：22353_kakuitsuka⟧: cultural homogenization

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{標準化|ひょうじゅんか}→標準化：20534_hyoujunka⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to standardize — neutral, technical; used for setting agreed specifications.
- ⟦{均一化|きんいつか}→均一化：08084_kinitsuka⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to make even / uniform — emphasizes evening out levels or amounts.
- ⟦{統一|とういつ}→統一：04551_touitsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to unify — broader; can mean bringing separate things under a single system or format.
- ⟦{一律|いちりつ}→一律：11204_ichiritsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to treat all cases alike / apply uniformly — often refers to applying the same rule to everyone.
- {没個性化|ぼつこせいか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to deprive of individuality — a more explicitly negative near-synonym.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{画一的|かくいつてき}→画一的：13594_kakuitsuteki⟧: uniform, standardized (adjective form, often with the same critical nuance)
- {画一主義|かくいつしゅぎ}: uniformism, one-size-fits-all approach
- ⟦{多様化|たようか}する→多様化する：25552_tayoukasuru⟧: to diversify — the direct opposite.

REGISTER:
Written and somewhat formal. Common in editorials, essays, and academic writing about education, urban planning, and culture. Not an everyday conversational verb.
